q: A consistency model is:
o: A contract specifying what values a read may return after writes
e: Contract between the data store and processes.

q: Which model requires an absolute global clock and is rarely achievable?
e: It is the theoretical upper bound.

q: In sequential consistency:
o: All processes see the same interleaving, not necessarily real-time order
e: Implementable, no global clock needed.

q: In causal consistency, concurrent writes:
o: Must be seen in the same order by all
May be seen in different orders by different processes
e: Only causally related writes need the same order.

q: DNS and many NoSQL stores use:
e: Replicas converge when updates stop.

q: Client-centric consistency models take the point of view of:
e: What one process sees across replicas.

q: You post a comment, refresh, and it is missing. Which guarantee is violated?
e: Your own write must be visible to you.

q: Your phone shows fewer emails than your laptop already showed. Which guarantee is violated?
e: Never go backward in time.

q: Push-based propagation suits:
o: High read-to-write ratio and need for freshness
e: Pull suits low read-to-write ratios.

q: A browser cache is an example of a:
e: Created at the client's request, temporary.

q: In CAP, Consistency means every read receives:
o: The most recent write or an error
e: Availability = a non-error response, maybe not latest.

q: ZooKeeper-style coordination services are classified as:
e: They reject requests on the minority side.

q: PACELC says that when there is NO partition you trade off:
e: Else: L or C.

q: With N=3 replicas, which quorum setting guarantees reads see the latest write?
A corrupted block caused by a bad disk sector is an example of a(n):
e: Fault (bad sector) -> error (corrupted block) -> failure (file unreadable).

q: Which failure type is the most severe?
e: Arbitrary, possibly malicious behaviour.

q: Retrying a transaction after a timeout is:
e: Physical = extra hardware; information = extra bits.

q: In a hierarchical process group, the main weakness is:
o: The coordinator is a single point of failure
e: Unless it is replaced automatically.

q: A heartbeat protocol suspects a process has failed when:
o: No heartbeat arrives within the timeout
e: Delays can cause false positives.

q: Gossip spreads information across N nodes in about:
e: Informed nodes roughly double each round.

q: Which semantics is safe only for idempotent operations?
e: Retries may execute the request more than once.

q: Atomic multicast guarantees a message is delivered to:
e: No partial delivery.

q: Total-order multicast means:
o: One sender's messages arrive in order
All members see all messages in the same order
e: FIFO is per sender; causal respects happened-before.

q: In 2PC, if any participant votes NO, the coordinator:
e: All-or-nothing atomicity.

q: 2PC blocks when:
o: The coordinator crashes after YES votes, before sending the decision
e: Participants cannot decide alone and hold locks.

q: 3PC adds which phase?
e: Vote -> prepare-to-commit (ACK) -> commit.

q: A drawback of 3PC compared with 2PC is:
e: Extra round and timeouts.

q: An access control list (ACL) is stored:
o: With the user as a token
e: A capability is held by the subject.

q: Kerberos-style tickets are used for:
e: Verifying who is making a request.
